limitations.lead: Six qualifications apply to this model. Each is stated in full and stays open; none changes the bottom line on its own.

items.title: EBITDA is the company’s own measure
items.label: Earnings
items.text: EBITDA as defined adds back items the company chooses. No independent adjustment was made, so leverage on a stricter measure would be higher.

items.title: FY23 cash interest is missing
items.label: Data
items.text: Cash interest for FY23 was not split out in the sources. Interest cover and free cash flow for that year are shown as n.a., not estimated.

items.title: FY22 inventories are missing
items.label: Data
items.text: The FY22 balance sheet in the sources does not show inventories separately. The figure is n.a. and FY22 working capital ratios are not stated.

items.title: No acquisitions or shareholder returns after FY25
items.label: Forecast
items.text: Both cases assume no acquisitions and forecast no dividends or buybacks. The company has made both in most years, so cash and leverage are likely to be worse than shown.

items.title: The downside case is a single scenario
items.label: Downside case
items.text: One traffic shock was modelled. It does not combine lower traffic with a loss of pricing power, and it assumes the 2028 maturities can still be refinanced.

items.title: Revolver terms are withheld
items.label: Downside case
items.text: The amount drawn and the terms of the revolving facility are shown to the deal team only. Liquidity under the downside case could not be measured.

items.title: Pension deficit
items.reason: No source in this run states the funded position of the pension plans.

items.title: Quarterly cash flow
items.reason: The sources give annual figures only, so no quarter-by-quarter path was built.

items.title: Months of liquidity, downside case
items.reason: The revolver terms are withheld, so the chart could not be drawn.
